translations.text: Her husband Elkanah said to her, “Hannah!” She said to him, “Here I am, my lord.” He said to her, “Why are you weeping? Why do you not eat? Why is your heart troubled? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

Her husband Elkanah said to her, “Do whatever seems good in your eyes. Stay here until you have weaned him, and may the Lord establish what has come from your mouth.” So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.

I chose your father’s house from all the tribes of Israel to serve me as priests, to approach my altar, to offer incense, and to wear the ephod before me. I gave your father’s house all the offerings made by fire by the Israelites for food.
You will continually look with sorrow upon all the good that the Lord, the God of Israel, will do, and there will never be an old man in your house.
I will raise up for myself a faithful priest who will do everything that is in my heart and in my soul. I will build him a lasting house, and he will walk before my anointed one all his days.
The Lord called again and said, “Samuel, Samuel!” Samuel got up and went to Eli a second time and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” He said, “I did not call you, my son. Go back and sleep.”
The Philistines called their priests, diviners, and wise men and said, “What shall we do with the ark of the Lord? Tell us what we should send with it when we return it to its place.”
The Philistines did so. They took two cows that had calved for the first time and yoked them to the cart, and they shut their calves inside.

The cows went straight along the road leading to Beth-shemesh. They followed a single path, toiling along, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines followed it as far as the borders of Beth-shemesh.
The people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valleys. They raised their eyes and saw the ark of the Lord, and they rejoiced as it approached.
The Israelites put away the Baals and the sacred groves of Ashtoreth and served him alone.
He would return to Ramathaim, for his house was there. There he judged Israel, and there he built an altar to the Lord.
All the men of Israel gathered and came to Samuel at Ramathaim.
The Lord said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of this people in what they have said to you, for it is not you they have rejected; they have rejected me from reigning over them.”
He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you will become his servants.
When these signs come upon you, do whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.
One of them answered and said, “Who is his father, if not Kish?” Therefore it became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
Samuel said to all the men of Israel, “Look, I have listened to your voice in everything you said to me, and I have appointed a king to reign over you.”

Here I stand. Testify about me before the Lord and before his anointed one. Whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I driven away? Have I oppressed any of you, or deprived anyone of anything? From whose hands have I taken payment or sandals? Testify about me, and I will repay you.
Now come forward, and I will plead the case against you before the Lord and recount to you all the righteous deeds that the Lord has done among you and among your fathers.
I said, ‘Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not entreated the Lord’s favor.’ So I forced myself and offered the burnt offerings.
The raiding force went out from the Philistine camp in three companies. One company headed along the road to Ophrah, toward the spring of Sogol.
And during the fighting at Michmash, no sword or spear was found in the hands of any of the people who were with Saul and his son Jonathan, but they were found with Saul and his son Jonathan.

Within the pass through which Jonathan sought to cross to the Philistine camp, among the ravines, there was a rocky crag on this side and a rocky crag on that side. The name of one was Bozez, and the name of the other was Seneh.
One crag was on the north, facing Michmash, and the other crag was on the south, facing Geba.
And Saul said, “I have sinned. But honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me so that I may worship the Lord your God.”
And Samuel did everything the Lord had told him and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city trembled when they met him and said, “Do you come in peace, seer?”
And the Israelites and the Philistines drew up their battle lines opposite one another, line facing line.
And the people spoke to him in the same words, saying, “This is what will be done for the man who kills him.”
And he turned away from him toward another and spoke in the same words, and the people answered him as they had before.
And Saul dressed David in his own garments, put a bronze helmet on his head, and clothed him in a coat of armor.
And the men of Israel returned from pursuing the Philistines and overran their camps.
And David acted wisely in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.
And Saul instructed his servants, saying, “Speak privately to David and say, ‘Look, the king is pleased with you, and all his men love you. Now become the king’s son-in-law.’”
“And I will go out and stand beside my father in the open, where you will be, and I will speak to my father about you. I will see what happens and tell you.”
And Michal took the household idols and placed them on the bed. She put a goat’s liver and a ball of hair at the head of the bed and covered it with a garment.
And Saul said to Michal, “Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he escaped?” And Michal said to Saul, “He himself said, ‘Let me go, or I will kill you.’”
And David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and spoke before Jonathan, saying, “What have I done? What is my offense, and what sin have I committed against your father, that he seeks my life?”
“And never withdraw your kindness from my household, not even when the Lord wipes out every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”
Jonathan answered his father Saul and said to him, “Why should he die? What has he done?”
And David took these words to heart and was greatly afraid of Achish, king of Gath.
And everyone in distress, everyone in debt, and everyone bitter in spirit gathered around him. He became their commander, and about four hundred men were with him.
Doeg the Syrian, who was in charge of Saul’s mules, answered and said, “I saw the son of Jesse come to Nob, to the priest Ahimelech son of Ahitub.”
And Saul said, “Listen, son of Ahitub.” And he said, “Here I am. Speak, my lord.”

And the king said to Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests of the Lord.” And Doeg the Syrian turned and slaughtered the priests of the Lord. On that day he killed three hundred and five men, all of whom wore the linen ephod.
And Abiathar told David that Saul had slaughtered all the priests of the Lord.
“May the Lord be judge and arbiter between me and you. May the Lord see and judge my case and secure justice for me against you.”
May God do this and more to David if by morning I leave anyone belonging to Nabal who urinates against a wall.
And in the morning, when Nabal had sobered up from the wine, his wife told him these things. His heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
And David’s servants came to Abigail at Carmel, spoke with her, and said, “David sent us to you to take you as his wife.”
And she rose, bowed with her face to the ground, and said, “Here is your maidservant, ready to serve by washing the feet of my lord’s servants.”

And David rose secretly and came to the place where Saul was staying. David saw the place where Saul slept, and there was Abner son of Ner, his army commander. Saul was sleeping in the covered wagon, and the army was encamped around him.

“And now, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If God has stirred you up against me, may your sacrifice give off a pleasing aroma. But if it is human beings, may they be cursed before the Lord, because today they have driven me away from having a place in the Lord’s inheritance, saying, ‘Go, serve foreign gods.’”
And Saul said, “I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will do you no harm, because my life is precious in your eyes. Today I have been foolish and very guilty.”
And the woman saw Samuel and cried out with a loud voice. The woman said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
And he would not eat, but his servants and the woman urged him, and he listened to them. He rose from the ground and sat on a seat.
And she set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and left that night.
And he took captive the women and everything in it, from small to great. They killed neither man nor woman, but took them captive and went on their way.
And they gave him a piece of a fig cake and two raisin cakes. He ate, and his spirit was strengthened by this, for he had eaten no bread and drunk no water for three days and three nights.

And David said to him, “Whose servant are you, and where are you from?” The young man said, “I am an Egyptian, the servant of an Amalekite man. My master abandoned me because I fell ill three days ago.”
And David took all the flocks and herds and drove them ahead of the spoil. He gave the spoil this name: “This is David’s spoil.”
And those in Jattir and Aroer, and those in Siphmoth, and those in Eshtemoa.
And all the valiant men rose and traveled all night. They took Saul’s body and the body of his son Jonathan from the wall of Beth-shan, brought them to Jabesh, and burned them there.
